== Biography ==
Eric Scott "Mancow" Muller (born June 21, 1966) is an American radio and television personality best known for his shock jock radio program, '''The Mancow Show'''. Known for his outspoken nature and controversial antics, Mancow has frequently courted controversy throughout his career, often engaging with conspiracy theories and contentious figures.

=== Career and Controversies ===
Mancow began his radio career in the late 1980s, eventually gaining notoriety for his provocative style. Over the years, he became embroiled in several controversies, including legal disputes and fines from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for content deemed indecent. His often inflammatory rhetoric and controversial stances have frequently drawn criticism from various groups and media watchdogs.

=== Conspiracies and Connections ===
Mancow has occasionally delved into conspiracy theories on his programs, discussing topics such as government cover-ups and alternative narratives on mainstream news events. His penchant for exploring conspiratorial themes has occasionally led to comparisons with other controversial media figures.

=== Connection with Alex Jones ===
Mancow has shared a notable connection with fellow radio host and conspiracy theorist Alex Jones. Over the years, they have appeared on each other's programs, discussing various conspiracy theories and controversial topics. Their alignment on certain issues has fostered a professional relationship, though Mancow has maintained a distinct persona marked by his unique style and approach to radio broadcasting.
